newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Two Cypriots killed, Britons injured in crash.
newsitem.headline: Two Cypriots killed, Britons injured in crash.

text.p: Two Cypriots were killed and two British servicemen injured in a morning collision on the outskirts of the military base of Dhekelia in Cyprus, police said.
Cypriots Demetris Yiallouros, 33, and Demetris Michael, 23, were killed when their vehicles were involved in a head on collision at 1.00 a.m. (2300 GMT) close to Larnaca town in south eastern Cyprus.
British soldiers Antony Moran and Christopher Burt, passengers in Yiallouros' taxi, were returning to base at the time.

Burt was seriously injured and taken to hospital in capital Nicosia. Moran, whose condition is less serious, is being treated at a military hospital at Akrotiri, the second British military base on the island.
A bases spokesman refused to elaborate on the nature of their injuries.
"Their evacuation to the UK is routine as and when their condition is stabilised," he added.
The two soldiers are stationed with the Kings Regiment in Dhekelia, one of two military bases Britain has retained on the island since independence in 1960.
Their ages and home towns were not released.
